text:
ada: quick heads-up — ran an nsys capture on the 8xA100 dedicated pool during the morning load test. seeing repeated 100–300ms JIT/compile hotspots right before the big kernel bursts, looks tied to Triton JIT + kernel cache misses. perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 :eyes:

mike: ugh that aligns with the latency spikes i saw in the route-level dashboard at 09:40 — p95 jumped ~120ms for ~2m window. did you capture kernel names?

ada: yep, grabbing the hot lines now. nsys summary (trimmed):
```
Kernel: triton_jit_compile  count=24  total_ms=4.1s  avg=170ms
Kernel: fw_conv_attention  count=240  total_ms=2.6s  avg=11ms
Kernel: softmax_kv_update   count=240  total_ms=1.2s  avg=5ms
Kernel: kv_prefetch         count=48   total_ms=560ms  avg=11.7ms
```
Looks like a handful of unique kernels trigger compile paths — triton_jit_compile dominates warmup.

sophia: are these happening per worker or per model variant? if kcache is per-process we might be recompiling after worker rotation.

ada: good question. trace shows kcache lookup misses spike when a new process starts: kcache_miss_rate ~0.28 for first 30s, then drops to ~0.02. so it's not per-request, it's per-worker cold start.

leo: that matches the dedicated pool churn during autoscale test — we spun up 6 new workers. each worker did a full compile of ~4 kernel variants for the small-seq path.

mike: possible mitigations: 1) persist kernel cache on disk between restarts (we have prototype), 2) prewarm on spawn with a minimal batch set, 3) bias kernel selection to choose already-compiled fallback kernels for first N requests.

ada: tried 2) locally — prewarm script that runs 10 dummy requests (batch sizes 1/4/8) reduced observed p95 warmup by ~70%. script: 
```
for bs in 1 4 8; do curl -X POST $SVC/inf -d @payload_bs${bs}.json; done
```
But it adds ~200ms to startup cost — acceptable if we do it asynchronously during scale-up.

perf-bot: perf-alert: compile-hotpath exceeded threshold on model=redwood-open-7B-lite at 2026-08-11T09:40:12Z. avg_jit_compile_ms=168, affected_workers=6.

sophia: can we change kernel selector heuristics to prefer cached kernels when sequence_len <=512 and tokens/prefix predictable? might trade a few ms per token for zero compile cost.

leo: yes, selector already has cost estimates. we could add a penalty for expected compile time and add a cache-hit boost. needs a small change in selector scoring function. i'll prototype.

mike: also worth checking if Triton's compiled artifacts have stable IDs — if artifacts differ due to minor config differences we get churn. check: environment CUDNN/Triton flags consistent across AMIs?

ada: verified AMI flags were identical, but our driver package had a minor version mismatch on 2 nodes — likely caused different compiled kernels. opening infra ticket to reprovision.

mike: for immediate relief, can we set a soft-cap of concurrent new-worker spawns during peak? reduces simultaneous JITs.

leo: yeah we can throttle spawn concurrency per-pool. tradeoff is slower scale-up.

ada: summary action items: (1) persist kcache between restarts (infra + perf), (2) add prewarm hooks for worker init, (3) update kernel selector scoring to penalize compile-heavy choices, (4) patch AMI to align driver versions, (5) throttle concurrent spawns as fallback. I'll open PRs/TF tasks for 1,4 and a small RFC for 3.

sophia: thanks — please attach the perfetto+nsys captures to the RFC so reviewers can see the timeline slices.

perf-bot: saved traces: s3://redwood-inference-perf/nsys/1908765432/trace.tar.gz

mike: one more ask: collect a tiny histogram of first-request latency vs request-number-per-worker (1..20). want to quantify warmup tail beyond anecdote.

ada: on it — will post numbers in this thread in ~30m.

leo: nice — if the histogram shows >5 warmup compilations per worker we need to rethink model sharding.

ada: posting quick numbers: first-request median=420ms, first-request p95=980ms, request #5 median=120ms, request #20 median=110ms, compile-events per-worker median=3.

mike: that median 3 compiles explains the 150–300ms spikes. ok let's move these into tickets. :+1:
